newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt could present budget on Sept 27 - source.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt could present budget on Sept 27 - source.

text.p: The Italian government could have a 1997 budget ready for parliament as early as September 27, a government source said following Friday's cabinet meeting.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government plans to cut next year's public sector borrowing requirement by 32.4 trillion lire.
Ministers in charge of drafting the package, made up of two-thirds reduced spending and one-third increased revenue, have been holding talks with cabinet colleagues all week on how to pare spending.
Sergio D'Antoni, leader of the CISL trades union, speaking to reporters after a meeting at the prime minister's office appeared to confirm the September 27 date.
He said a national conference on employment involving government, unions and employers due to have been held that day in Naples had been brought forward to September 25 and 26.
Political sources noted the September 27 date would allow Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi to attend the G7 meeting at the end of the month in Washington.
Under Italian law, the budget package must be presented to parliament by September 30. Both chambers then have until December 31 to approve it.
